title: The state of China's memory industry in 2026
summary: China's memory output comes from CXMT and YMTC, a few smaller fabs, and Chinese Samsung and SK hynix plants, but no Chinese maker has HBM in volume yet.
body: China’s homegrown memory comes largely from two companies, CXMT for DRAM and YMTC for 3D NAND, and both are booming. CXMT’s Oct. 30 quarterly report shows a nine-month net profit of ¥132.0 billion ($19.6 billion), against a ¥5.28 billion ($785 million) loss a year earlier, on revenue more than eight times as high, at ¥269.0 billion ($40.0 billion). YMTC’s numbers, just for Q1, are at ¥47.04 billion ($7.0 billion) in revenue and ¥33.38 billion ($5.0 billion) in profit attributable to shareholders, more than double 2025. Both are expanding and adding fabs, and each is edging into the other’s products. No Chinese manufacturer can yet produce high-bandwidth memory (HBM) in volume, though. HBM is the stacked DRAM that AI accelerators depend on, and currently the U.S. bars Samsung, SK hynix, and Micron from selling it into China. CXMT’s prospectus lists no HBM project , though its HBM3E is reportedly in risk production , an early run before the process is fully qualified. Huawei designs its own HBM but doesn’t say who makes it. Memory is a commodity, so the story is in the wafers. title: Google DeepMind AI engineers conjure mathematical proof of Signal's encryption protocol
summary: Google DeepMind AI engineers conjure mathematical proof of Signal's encryption protocol — AlphaProof Code framework powered human-bot cooperation for speedy work
body: A team at Google's DeepMind AI labs has performed a complete formal proof of the code that implements the encryption mechanism for the Signal private chat application. The scientists call their procedure AlphaProof Code and claim it can be applied to other situations requiring complete end-to-end verification of computer code, meaning Signal is safe, and you can find the full paper and the code repository detailing the proof. More explicitly, the team reviewed an Arm-compiled version of libsignal, the library that the Signal application itself incorporates and uses, with some minimal scaffolding around it. Note that the verification wasn't done against the source code: it was purposely executed against an AArch64 binary , meaning the method can be reused for future verifications of other software. In a similar vein to the AI labs' work on mathematics, the bulk of the work was done in Lean , a purpose-built language for formal proofs. There's a key difference for this effort, though. Lean is primarily used to prove the underlying math in algorithms, which in this case would be the specifications for Signal's encryption. title: US DOJ touts "largest-ever" crackdown on scammers across the globe as it seizes 14,000 devices and $17 billion in illicit funds
summary: The U.S. Department of Justice has announced that the largest anti-scam push in its history has resulted in more than $8 billion in intended victim losses being recovered, leading to more than 800 defendants being charged.
body: The United States Department of Justice announced today that more than 800 defendants have been charged and over $8 billion in intended victim losses have been recovered in what it describes as the "largest ever" crackdown on scammers and fraudsters in its history. The charges have led to over 400 cases, filed across 85 federal districts, with outcomes including extraditions, guilty pleas, and prison sentences for those involved. "We are not just going after individual scammers," Fox News reports U.S. Attorney General Todd Blanche as saying. "We are dismantling the criminal networks that have been stealing from the American people for far too long." The push follows President Donald Trump's executive order from March, which required a government-wide crackdown on the kinds of fraud and predatory schemes that people fall victim to each and every day across the country. FBI Director Kash Patel also gave details of Operation Blackout, an interagency project that targets international fraudsters running centralized facilities. title: Saudi OpenAI eavesdropper who bugged company office had hundreds of private recordings
summary: Prosecutors found dozens of recordings of OpenAI meetings and conversations recorded from a covert listening device inside one of the company's conference rooms.
body: Last month, a former O penAI employee with ties to Saudi Arabia was arrested for bugging conference rooms in the company . Today, Bloomberg reports that prosecutors in the case uncovered hundreds of recordings, dozens of which were meetings and conversations dating as far back as September. Prosecutors believe some recordings may contain sensitive information that can be regarded as trade secrets, the dispersion of which could be a threat to US national security. In October, we covered how Abdulrahman Alfozan, a former OpenAI employee, was arrested for installing a covert listening device behind the company's executive conference room television using a Seeed Xiao ESP32-S3. The device was discovered days later, with investigations linking it to Alfozan and subsequently leading to his arrest and removal from the company.
